entertainment.title: Sylvester Stallone was once broke and lonely — before Henry Winkler changed his life
entertainment.summary: In his memoir, "The Steps," the "Rocky" icon recalls crossing paths with the future "Happy Days" star on the set of 1974's "The Lords of Flatbush."
entertainment.body:
Before Sylvester Stallone became a Hollywood heavyweight, he was a broke, lonely actor living in a cramped New York City walk-up apartment with few friends to lean on — until Henry Winkler came along.

In his memoir, “The Steps,” the “Rocky” icon recalls crossing paths with the future “Happy Days” star on the set of 1974’s “The Lords of Flatbush.”

Though Stallone joked they were polar opposites — Winkler, a Yale graduate, and Stallone from “the college of what’s the matter [with] you” — the two forged an instant bond.

For Winkler, it didn’t take long to see Stallone’s fierce determination to make it in Hollywood. It was a drive he witnessed firsthand when he visited his co-star’s home on Lexington Avenue for the first time.

“He was living there with his first wife and their Bullmastiff, who had more slobber than the Atlantic Ocean,” Winkler recalled to Fox News Digital.

“He painted his windows black so that he would never be bothered by what time of day it was. He wouldn’t be influenced by time. Instead, he just wrote and wrote. And from the minute we met on the set of a movie in which we made no money whatsoever, you could see him. You could see his drive. You could see there was something so special, so funny, so articulate coming out of this, ‘I’m going to eat you for breakfast.’ And it only continued.”

“If you listen to Sly Stallone, you quickly realize he’s a philosopher,” Winkler shared.

“You would never put the two together, but it’s true. And he’s so open. His upbringing would put any man or woman down. It would put them in a corner shaking for the rest of their life. But his motto is ‘keep on punching’ and it’s true. He kept on punching. And it’s been an honor to be his friend.”

entertainment.title: Denis Villeneuve Pledges Traditional, “Unapologetic” Bond: “Not Here to Change the DNA”
entertainment.summary: The director teases a classic approach to his Amazon MGM film starring Robert Pattinson: "I love the way the character behaves."
entertainment.body:
Logo text Denis Villeneuve says his highly anticipated reboot of the James Bond franchise isn’t going to back away from the “unapologetic” traits of the iconic character.

The Dune: Part Three director teased his vision of 007 in a new interview and suggested that he’s a traditionalist when it comes to portraying Ian Fleming’s suave, seductive, killer spy.

“I love traditions,” Villeneuve told Time . “I love the unapologetic way the character behaves, the panache. I’m not here to change the DNA of James Bond. I’m here to embrace it, to bring it to the world of today. I’m a hardcore James Bond fan, and I want other fans to have fun watching my film. Of course, it will be tainted by my sensibility. But I wake up every morning with a stupid smile because it’s a world of pure cinematic pleasure.” Related Stories Movies 'Twilight' Director Reveals Robert Pattinson Inspired James Bond Line in 2008 Film: "We Were Seeing the Future" Movies 'Avengers: Doomsday' Eyes $270M Opening as 'Dune: Part Three' Also Heads for Big Start

That said, the director added, “I don’t want to talk too much about Bond because it’s still in the oven cooking. This stage of the process is my favorite part because everything is possible.”

The comments are interesting because of the cultural debate that’s surrounded Bond in recent years, and how the later Daniel Craig films attempted to wrestle with the question of how the often sexist cinematic character dating back to the 1960s should operate in the modern age.

How much Villeneuve was thinking of Pattinson during his comments is unclear — the interview was conducted one week before The Batman actor was publicly announced as the new Bond .

Meanwhile, speculation has shifted to who will play the film’s villain, with oddsmakers thinking Tom Hardy has a strong shot (indeed, given Pattinson’s slight frame, choosing a physically imposing villain would make for a nicely formidable antagonist). Director Danny Boyle — who was originally tapped to direct No Time to Die — has said that “beginning to talk about Jack O’Connell as a possible villain.” O’Connell was previously considered a contender to play Bond himself .

Boyle told The Alchemy podcast that both Pattinson and O’Connell have a similar quality. “They have that thing [where] you want to watch them,” he said. “And it’s impossible to quantify what it is; otherwise we’d all buy it for ourselves. But it’s just there and you want to follow them.”

entertainment.title: Justin Timberlake Explains Why He Was ‘Reluctant’ to Make New Docuseries During ‘Tonight Show’ Interview
entertainment.summary: The singer told Jimmy Fallon why he was initially hesitant to open up about his private life in the upcoming four-part documentary series.
entertainment.body:
Justin Timberlake is opening up about what convinced him to share a more personal side of himself in his upcoming documentary.

During an appearance on The Tonight Show on Thursday (Nov. 26), the 45-year-old pop superstar told host Jimmy Fallon that he was initially hesitant to pull back the curtain on his private life for Timberlake , a four-part documentary series premiering on Apple TV on Dec. 11.

“I was really reluctant to do it,” Timberlake told Fallon, noting that he’s always been a pretty private person. But his relationship with director Fisher Stevens eventually helped change his mind, with their conversations encouraging him to open up about parts of his life he hadn’t previously discussed.

“When Fisher first approached me to do this, I was reluctant because I was like, ‘I don’t wanna talk about myself,’” Timberlake continued. But as they continued talking, he found himself “searching for something that was beneath the surface a little more.”

The “Can’t Stop the Feeling!” singer also reflected on how his experiences over the past five years have shaped him.

“You just never know what somebody’s going through, right?” Timberlake said. “And I think I kind of decided, maybe people see my life from the outside and it’s like, ‘Wow!’ But everybody’s going through something, and I think I’ve gone through a lot in the last five years that I feel like has made me a better human and a better father, a better husband, a better friend.”

Timberlake said making the docuseries proved “to be really cathartic,” and he hopes his willingness to be vulnerable will resonate with viewers who may be navigating similar experiences.

“Maybe people see my life from the outside and it’s like, ‘Wow!’ But everybody’s going through something,” the singer said. “Maybe I can be a beacon of light for whoever’s watching.”

entertainment.title: Amelia Dimoldenberg Tears Up in Final Episode of ‘Chicken Shop Date’
entertainment.summary: The comedian and host brought her long-running YouTube series to an end with an emotional interview with therapist Esther Perel
entertainment.body:
Don’t cry because it’s over. Amelia Dimoldenberg aired the emotional final episode of her long-running YouTube interview series Chicken Shop Date , concluding the show by wiping away a few genuine tears.

Instead of enlisting a celebrity to join her on the series, Dimoldenberg opted to make acclaimed Belgian relationship therapist Esther Perel her guest for the finale. “For my final date, I wanted to do something different,” the host shared on social media . “I wanted to end Chicken Shop Date by showing another side of myself, in the most truthful way I could think of.”

For the episode, Dimoldenberg shed her usual persona and got real with Perel, explaining why she had decided to bring the show to its conclusion.

“I think I have to end the show to meet somebody,” Dimoldenberg told Perel. She added, “I definitely would love to meet someone that wasn’t a celebrity, if I’m being honest. It seems very intense to go out with a celebrity.”

Perel encouraged Dimoldenberg to imagine she is having a conversation with Chicken Shop Date itself, which leads to an emotional monologue and a tearful farewell.

“Thank you for allowing me to be where I am today,” Dimoldenberg told Perel as the show. “I’ve learned so much. I’ve grown up so much and I’ve had so much fun. But I feel now trapped in a cage of my own making and I’m ready to try something else. I never thought I would be able to say goodbye. I thought you would be part of my life forever.”

She added, “It was quite a shock to realize that doesn’t need to be the case. And now I feel kind of liberated in the farewell, in thinking there could be another path.”

entertainment.title: ‘Big Brother’ alum Paul Abrahamian accused of illegally owning and transporting human remains in wild exposé
entertainment.summary: Customs agents allegedly intercepted a package with a young boy's mummified skull heading to Abrahamian's New York address, according to a bombshell article.
entertainment.body:
“Big Brother” alum Paul Abrahamian was accused of illegally sourcing human remains in a Los Angeles Times exposé published Wednesday.

The article linked Abrahamian, 33, to a Dec. 13, 2022, incident that involved Buenos Aires customs agents intercepting a US-bound package that appeared to contain a human skull.

Inside the package, authorities allegedly found a Spider-Man mask stashed above a mummified skull of a young boy wrapped in gauze and a wool cap.

The boy’s eyelashes and a tuft of his red-orange hair were still attached to the skull, per the LA Times.

The skull was sent to a nonprofit scientific organization for further testing, but a positive identification was unable to be made.

The Argentine Federal Police reportedly discovered that the sender used the fake name Gustavo Damami, which did not appear in any Argentine records.

However, the addressee listed was a “Paul Adrahamian” at an apartment complex in Brooklyn. One of Abrahamian’s former girlfriends confirmed to the LA Times that she was living with Abrahamian at that same address at the time.

Abrahamian told the LA Times in a statement, “The situation referenced in Argentina is inaccurate. I had no involvement in that matter, and it does not reflect my work in any way.”

entertainment.title: The Only Two Gilligan's Island Actors Who Appeared On Baywatch's Homage Episode
entertainment.summary: The two notable characters from "Gilligan's Island" popped up on an episode of the original "Baywatch" series and they were still castaways.
entertainment.body:
Directed by Douglas Schwartz and written by Lloyd Schwartz — who both have familial ties with legendary series creator Sherwood Schwartz — "Now Sit Right Back And You'll Hear A Tale" saw Denver and Wells reprising their roles of Gilligan and Mary Ann Summers. How is that even possible, you ask? Well, it all worked out thanks to the "it was all a dream" trope.

The plot centers on Eddie (Billy Warlock), who bumps his head and slips into a fever dream where he and Shauni (Erika Eleniak) find themselves shipwrecked on a mysterious island alongside the actual Gilligan and Mary Ann. In the dream, other "Baywatch" characters eventually make their way to the island and begin to take on characteristics of some of the other castaways, with Officer Garner Ellerbee (Gregory Alan Williams) becoming the new Skipper, Captain Don Thorpe (Monte Markham) filling in as the billionaire Thurston Howell III, and Shauni becoming the new Ginger.

The Baywatch Company/YouTube The cast seemingly had a blast, with Eleniak even taking to her X (formerly Twitter) account to hail it as her favorite "Baywatch" episode. Even Wells looked back on the guest spot fondly. "That was a good experience," she told the Television Academy , while adding, "It was fun. I think they had a Black Skipper. It was cute."

While the cast may have had a great time, the "Baywatch" fanbase wasn't too wild about the crossover episode. "Now Sit Right Back And You'll Hear A Tale" has a divisive 5.2 score on IMDb. In one of the more positive-leaning reviews, IMDb user paultapner wrote, "You will either find this stupid and unfunny beyond belief. Or you will like its ambition and originality and enjoy it for that. I went for the latter." On the negative side, user TheFearmakers called the episode "so bad" and "not funny," while adding, "It's not so bad seeing Bob Denver and Wells reprising their roles ." User bombersflyup ripped the episode to shreds, calling it "unbearable," while adding, "the show's already stupid, it can't intentionally be. Couldn't sit through this one."

"Baywatch" wasn't actually the first TV series to reunite the stranded castmates. In 1987, Denver and Wells, along with Russell Johnson and Alan Hale Jr., reprised their roles for an episode of "ALF" titled "The Ballad of Gilligan's Island," which, like "Baywatch," used the dream gimmick to teleport ALF to the famed uncharted desert isle where he meets the beloved castaways.

entertainment.title: 5 TV Shows To Watch If You Like 12 12 12
entertainment.summary: If Apple TV's heist series "12 12 12" has you craving similar thrills, here are five other shows you should add to your watch list.
entertainment.body:
Courtesy of Apple TV Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Apple TV's prestige heist thriller "12 12 12" is made for viewers who love plot machinations and cat-and-mouse suspense. Anthony Mackie plays disgraced FBI agent Jack Strickland, who's on the trail of master thief Paul Galvin (Jamie Dornan) after he pulls off a bank heist in Europe. The story is broken up into three intertwining points of view related to the 12 months it takes to plan a heist, the 12 hours it takes to execute a heist, and the 12-day window in which the thief needs to be caught.

"12 12 12" has a lot of fun with its ticking-clock storytelling device, using it to show character backgrounds and motivations. TV shows that operate on a similar wavelength — like those that use nonlinear narratives — can be tricky to pull off. But if there's a solid hook to grab viewers, a goal for the characters that's challenging but not too complicated to follow, and a satisfying payoff at the end, you have yourself a successfully entertaining operation.

If you're all in on "12 12 12," here are five other shows you should add to your watchlist.

Netflix "Kaleidoscope" is an eight-episode Netflix miniseries that follows a crew, led by mastermind Leo Pap ( played by "Breaking Bad" star Giancarlo Esposito ), planning to steal $7 billion in bearer bonds from a Manhattan bank. The story is loosely inspired by a real event where $70 billion in bonds actually did go missing from a New York City bank during Hurricane Sandy in 2012. Like with "12 12 12," the creators have their own clever way of presenting the narrative.

The story covers a 24-year span. Each episode is titled with a color that represents a different point in time related to the heist. For example, the episode "Yellow" takes place six weeks before the heist, the episode "Violet" takes place 24 years before the heist, and so on. Each viewer who streamed "Kaleidoscope" would see the episodes in a different order with a different starting point, creating a unique viewing experience.

According to Netflix, they wanted viewers to take their own path into the story — similar to the members of a heist crew — and arrive together at the same time the heist is going down in the gripping "Kaleidoscope" finale . "The idea is that when you watch the 'White' [finale] episode, you're learning true answers to things that have been hinted about beforehand and afterward," creator Eric Garcia told Netflix's Tudum . "You really find out everybody's true motivations. It's almost like a skeleton key."

entertainment.body:
Japanese anime master Masaaki Yuasa’s new studio, ame pippin, has revealed first look images and a clip from the highly-anticipated animated feature Daisy’s Life , a tale of grief and healing now delayed to a 2027 theatrical release in Japan.

The first title from Yuasa’s new studio ame pippin unveiled images to The Hollywood Reporter of the main characters from the animated adaptation of Banana Yoshimoto’s novel, The Life of Daisy, and original illustrations by Yoshitomo Nara. In one image, the young protagonist Daisy and her closest friend, Dahlia, are standing together in a lush forest. Related Stories Movies Golden Globes Category Chaos: When 'The Drama' Is a Comedy... Movies Golden Globes: 'I Play Rocky' Submitted as Comedy (Exclusive)

The second image shows both animated characters seated together at the roots of a tree, bonding over yakisoba, a Japanese stir-fried noodle dish. Their friendship helps frame the story of Daisy, who, as a child, lost her mother, her only family, in a tragic accident and now grieves that death as she struggles with a new life with her aunt. Studio ame pippin on Thursday unveiled a short clip from Daisy’s Life on X.

“On a long, lonely night during the rainy season, she (Daisy) plays the recorder by herself. As if drawn by the sound, Dahlia appears and becomes the friend who supports Daisy through her isolation. Years later, while Daisy is living and working at her aunt and uncle’s yakisoba restaurant, a letter arrives from Brazil. It speaks of the mysterious connection between two lonely souls separated by distance and time,” a synopsis from the producers of Daisy’s Life states about the young girl’s life changing one sleepless night.

The film is the first animated feature from ame pippin, the animation studio founded by Yuasa in 2025. Daisy’s Life also marks the first animated adaptation of books by Yoshimoto, a popular Japanese writer whose literary work has been published in 30 countries, with over seven million copies in print.

Published in 2000, Yashimoto’s The Life of Daisy novel centers around Daisy (Hinagiku) and explores the themes of death and loss through Daisy’s relationships with her mother and childhood best friend, Dahlia.

Director Yuasa is known for classic films like The Tatami Galaxy and Ping Pong the Animation, and in 2013 co-founded Science SARU with Eunyoung Choi. He directed an episode of Adventure Time and The Night Is Short, Walk on Girl.

entertainment.title: Denis Villeneuve “Deeply Disappointed” Disney Put ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Against ‘Dune 3’
entertainment.summary: The director breaks silence on going head-to-head against Marvel's titan on "Dunesday."
entertainment.body:
Logo text Everybody has found it pretty cute, if slightly baffling, that expected box-office heavyweights Dune: Part Three and Avengers: Doomsday are opening on the same day (Dec. 18).

But Dune franchise director Denis Villeneuve isn’t amused by going head-to-head with the Marvel titan.

Villeneuve explains in a new interview that he was “deeply disappointed” by the “Dunesday” scheduling, but that Warner Bros. was basically trapped in the slot because the studio had successfully secured an exclusive run on IMAX screens for Dune 3 through the December holidays. Related Stories Movies 'Avengers: Doomsday' Eyes $270M Opening as 'Dune: Part Three' Also Heads for Big Start Movies 'Avengers: Doomsday' Final Trailer Shows Major X-Men Moment

“Listen, I will be honest,” he told Time . “The first Dune came out at the end of the pandemic. We made a great box office in a very rough environment. But we had the winds against us. Then the second movie, same thing. We were meant to release in the fall, and we had to release at the end of winter because of the two Hollywood strikes. We had success, but it was not easy. The third time, I said to myself, ‘Finally, there is no pandemic, no strike in sight. We will have a normal release.’ Then Disney put the biggest franchise of all time against us. I’m no fool. Those movies are a mammoth.”

“So I was deeply disappointed,” continued the director. “But we had committed to this date, to IMAX. It was impossible to move. So I accepted my fate, praying to the gods of cinema. Dune is not a mammoth like the Avengers, but it’s a sexy little animal that has a lot of firepower, and I hope we will survive. It could be one of the biggest box-office weekends of all time because of both movies. Am I in competition with the Avengers ? Absolutely not. It’s a T. rex. But I stand proud because I think the film delivers.”

Both films have notably broken presales records . Dune: Part Three has reportedly bested Warner Bros. all-time presales record, selling more than $30 million worth of tickets for IMAX screens alone (the studio hasn’t released its own all-theater presales numbers). But Doomsday has recently surpassed $100 million and has received the highest initial opening-weekend forecast in NRG tracking history ($270 million). So there’s no world in which both films aren’t big hits, but also no world in which Doomsday doesn’t clock Dune on opening weekend.

entertainment.summary: A new wellness resort is attracting a glittery crowd with outré longevity offerings. Rectal ozone therapy, anyone?
entertainment.body:
Pampering spa getaways are so passé. The reinvented power trip? Longevity-centered five-star resorts that zero in on preventive medicine and rigorous cutting-edge health-optimization treatments. Think Benjamin Button-like cellular reprogramming and biotech breakthroughs that promise to help rewind biological aging in the elite quest to amp up health span.

Once confined largely to Switzerland, top-tier medi- wellness destinations are moving closer to Hollywood. Most notable among them is SHA Mexico, which opened in 2024 on a beachfront stretch of Costa Mujeres, north of Cancún. The flagship avant-garde longevity clinic, SHA Spain, launched in 2008 in the coastal town of L’Albir, has welcomed pro athletes, royalty, supermodels and such stars as Barbra Streisand (for repeat visits), Demi Moore, Monica Bellucci, Javier Bardem and Penélope Cruz, Lily James, Madonna and Marisa Tomei. Now names like Dakota Johnson, Kate Moss, Jack Black, Pink, model Candice Swanepoel and Lake Bell are on the guest list at the Mexican outpost. Related Stories Lifestyle The 5 Best Red Light Therapy Panels for Improving Your Health At-Home Lifestyle Jennifer Aniston Joins Boyfriend Jim Curtis For Chat About Health, Wellness and Hypnotherapy

Calling to mind The Jetsons ’ Googie-style home in Orbit City, the futuristic design, by Mexican architecture studio Sordo Madaleno, was aptly inspired by the human genome. Exclusive to this location is a bank of stem cells, unveiled in June, ethically sourced from embryonic tissues for medical and aesthetic cellular regeneration therapies that target autoimmune disease, muscle injuries, sleep apnea, aging skin and more. (At SHA Spain, therapies use the patient’s own stem cells; these donor-derived regenerative treatments are not yet approved in the U.S. or Europe for the uses described.) Treatments are administered through intravenous infusions, nebulizer inhalation and targeted injection; exosome facials inject the cell-derived donor particles directly into the face.

“These therapies reprogram the body’s natural mechanisms to heal and rejuvenate from the inside out,” says Dr. Andrea Márquez, head of SHA’s regenerative medicine, explaining that aging or inflamed cellular systems need a reboot.

A Cell Regeneration Therapy bed with a “human regenerator device” is said to boost energy, support physical recovery and promote anti-aging benefits by surrounding the body with a field of electrically charged particles.

entertainment.title: The Killers Dave Keuning Reveals He Suffered ‘Major Stroke’: ‘I Am Alive and Well’
entertainment.summary: "The doctors said I had a 40% chance or survival and I would have disabilities after, but by some miracle I am fine"
entertainment.body:
The Killers ‘ bassist Dave Keuning revealed that he was recently hospitalized after suffering a “major stroke.” In an Instagram post on Thursday, Keuning shared a photo of him with his three-month-old daughter Odette and disclosed that he is “alive and well” after his medical emergency.

“Two weeks ago, I had a major stroke, and thanks to my wife acting fast, I went straight to the hospital and into surgery,” Keuning wrote. “The first hour after a stroke is critical when it comes to getting to the hospital. I had a blood clot in my brain that cut off the blood supply to the entire right side of my brain. By the time I arrived at the hospital, I was blind in one eye and had lost function on my left side, but I still wasn’t able to realize I was having a stroke. The doctors said I had a 40% chance or survival and I would have disabilities after, but by some miracle I am fine.”

He continued, “And yes I can play guitar just as good as before. It was the first thing I checked when I woke up from surgery. I feel extremely fortunate that I am alive and well, and that I can use my hands and feet and talk just like before. I am thankful for my wife, my son, my daughter, and all of my bandmates, who I feel closer to than ever.”

If you've read Diana Gabaldon's "Outlander" books, the final moments of the "Outlander: Blood of My Blood" Season 2 finale likely got your mind whirling. And if you didn't, please allow us to explain what might be happening.

In the novels, Jamie (played by Sam Heughan in the original series) has an older brother named William. We don't meet him in the course of the books — he died when he was 11 — but Jamie warmly remembers that William carved him a wooden snake and used to call Jamie "Sawny."

Is William Beauchamp going to turn out to be William Fraser? And while there's no blood link, does that make Jamie's older brother also Claire's (Caitríona Balfe) younger brother?!

We took our query about this (and more!) directly to executive producers Matthew B. Roberts and Maril Davis. Read on to hear what they had to say about William and another canon character who may have shown up in the time-travel drama's season finale.

entertainment.title: 5 TV Shows To Watch If You Like Kim Kardashian's All's Fair
entertainment.summary: If you're loving All's Fair, Hulu's campy legal series starring Kim Kardashian, then you'll want to watch these five shows with the same over-the-top drama.
entertainment.body:
Disney/Ser Baffo Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover The Ryan Murphy TV series "All's Fair" isn't known for its glowing reviews — in fact, quite the opposite. The campy legal drama premiered with an almost unprecedented 0% on Rotten Tomatoes, a poor showing that may have actually inspired some viewers to tune in. TVLine's own Andy Swift described "All's Fair" as a "gay fever dream" saved by Sarah Paulson's "phenomenally unhinged" performance.

Indeed, there's plenty to love about the show, which stars Paulson alongside heavy hitters Glenn Close, Niecy Nash-Betts, Naomi Watts, Teyana Taylor, and Kim Kardashian. The series follows a group of female lawyers who start their own firm to focus on high-profile divorce cases. "All's Fair" is high camp, with outrageous outfits, hilariously deranged insults, flashy speeches, and soap opera plotlines. It's trashy legal fun, and frankly, there's not much on TV quite like it. However, if you've had your fill of the show and are looking for something else to scratch that itch, we've got you covered. Here are five shows to watch if you like "All's Fair."

ABC Though they have their own distinct styles, both Ryan Murphy and Shonda Rhimes know how to spin a mighty fine yarn. The two showrunners are both known for soapy melodrama and diverse casting practices. Fans of "All's Fair" should definitely check out "How to Get Away with Murder," an over-the-top legal drama starring acclaimed actor Viola Davis. The show was created by Peter Nowalk, while Rhimes served as executive producer.

Davis plays Annalise Keating, a Philadelphia defense attorney and law professor who teaches Criminal Law 100, colloquially known as How to Get Away with Murder. Each year, Annalise picks five students from the class to intern at her law firm. In addition to figuratively learning how to get away with murder, the students also get thrown into a criminal conspiracy when they are forced to cover up an actual murder. The show is deliciously dramatic, featuring outlandish plotlines and some powerful acting from Davis. If you like "All's Fair," you'll appreciate the series' heightened emotional landscape and its many twists and turns.

CBS "All's Fair" is campy TV of the highest order, and it never pretends to have loftier aims than pure entertainment. If you're looking for a show that weaves its legal storylines with a little more intelligence (though never forgets to have fun), our mandatory ruling is that you watch "The Good Fight," a brilliant series from Robert and Michelle King. A spinoff of the equally excellent "The Good Wife," the show follows Diane Lockhart (Christine Baranski), a veteran lawyer who goes to work for a prominent, Black-owned law firm in Chicago after losing her job and her life savings.

sports.title: Aaron Rodgers got no support from the Thanksgiving broadcasts
sports.summary: The day after former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers went on TV and aired dirty laundry from the Pittsburgh locker room, none of the former quarterbacks (or other former players) who appear on TV supported him.
sports.body:
Across the board, the reaction from the NFL’s analysts and broadcasters was negative.

Former Steelers quarterback and Fox analyst Terry Bradshaw went off . Fox’s Michael Strahan agreed that Rodgers shouldn’t have gone public with his complaints — calling him a “narcissist” and a “rich jerk” and a “rich bad teammate.”

Fox’s Howie Long said that the moment “defines who [Rodgers] is.”

“He’s a guy that I think picked the wrong sport,” Long said. “He probably should have played tennis.”

Fox’s Rob Gronkowski said that, even if a contender loses its starting quarterback, there’s “too much smoke” to justify bringing Rodgers in.

The CBS pregame crew offered similar views . Nate Burleson said Rodgers “ didn’t handle this right .” Bill Cowher said he hates to see a Hall of Famer go out this way . Russell Wilson said, “It’s about Aaron Rodgers’s legacy. . . . If I’m his family members, if I’m somebody close to him, I’m his significant other, whatever it may be. ‘ Is this how you want to go out? ’ After all the success he’s had, is this how you want to go out? . . . This is a disappointment.”

During the Eagles-Cowboys game, Fox’s Tom Brady criticized Rodgers for violating the “ sanctity ” of the locker room.

The irony, if I’m using the term correctly (I never know), is that Rodgers has previously railed about leaks from the locker room.

sports.title: Broncos, under Bo Nix, are much better at home than on the road
sports.summary: Lost in the ongoing drama in Pittsburgh is that they play the 8-2 Broncos today.
sports.body:
After playing 23 games in Denver, Nix has a 20-3 record with 43 touchdown passes and averaging 242.6 passing yards per game. Playing 23 games elsewhere, the Broncos are 13-10, with Nix throwing 27 touchdowns and averaging 195.9 passing yards per game.

The Steelers, in contrast, are 4-0 at home this year and 2-4 on the road.

With the forecast for the game similar to the conditions that played out in Buffalo on Thursday night, that could even things out, from a talent standpoint. And it could give the Steelers a chance to rebound from two days of total dysfunction with a season-altering win.

However it goes, the pressure is on Steelers coach Mike McCarthy. The best way to turn the page is to win. A loss (particularly an ugly one) will give even more credence to the things Aaron Rodgers said publicly on Wednesday.

sports.title: Brian Schottenheimer on failed fourth-down try: "I trust our quarterback and our offense"
sports.summary: The Eagles' path to erasing a 31-10 third-quarter deficit included many favorable twists and turns.
sports.body:
With 55 seconds left — and with the Eagles having no timeouts — the Cowboys faced fourth and one from the Philadelphia 39. After attempting to get the Eagles to jump offside, the Cowboys took a timeout and decided to go for it.

The Cowboys lined up in shotgun formation. Quarterback Dak Prescott looked to the right, presumably to connect on a slant to receiver CeeDee Lamb. Lamb was jammed hard by cornerback Quinyon Mitchell. Prescott waited for Lamb to get free. When Prescott decided to pursue another option, he was sacked.

The play lost nine yards, giving the Eagles the ball at their own 48.

Why not punt? Why not force quarterback Joe Milton III to drive into field-goal range, with less than 50 seconds to play and no timeouts?

Coach Brian Schottenheimer was asked about the decision after the game.

“Really felt good about the drive we had going, and felt really good that we were gonna put the game away there,” Schottenheimer told reporters. “And I wanted the ball in Dak’s hands. And, unfortunately, we weren’t able to make it work.”

“All the time,” he said. “Not in that situation. Absolutely not in that situation.”

“I trust our quarterback and our offense,” Schottenheimer said.

sports.title: Dan Campbell on calling late timeouts: I was hoping for a "chance for rebuttal"
sports.summary: With 2:34 to play on Thursday, the Lions had the ball on the Chicago 39.
sports.body:
But the drive ended when coach Dan Campbell decided to go for it on fourth and four from the Chicago 33, instead of attempting a 51-yard field goal that would have stretched the lead to six.

Yes, the Bears would have gotten the ball back with more than two minutes to play, if Campbell had opted to kick (and if kicker Jake Bates had made it). Yes, a touchdown (and an extra point) would have won the game. By not converting, the Bears had a chance to play for overtime or, if they could gain enough ground, a game-winning touchdown.

After the game, Campbell addressed the decision to go for it on fourth down.

“I don’t regret that, you know?” Campbell said. “I wish we would have made that. But, listen, sometimes that happens, you know?”

While that decision becomes the obvious focus of postgame scrutiny, a subsequent decision deserves some focus, too: As the Bears drove for what ultimately was the game-winning touchdown with three seconds left, Campbell called a pair of timeouts.

He called one after the Bears got a first down at the Detroit 31, with 1:12 to play. He called another after the Bears got a first down at the Detroit 21, with 52 seconds to play.

At the time, the Bears had only one timeout. Given the Thanksgiving Day debacle from 2024, when the Bears got greedy and blew their shot at a field goal that would have forced overtime (and coach Matt Eberflus got fired the next day), they undoubtedly wouldn’t have gotten cute as the final minute ticked away.

Two years later, those two timeouts allowed the Bears to run the clock all the way down to the last few seconds before taking the lead.

sports.title: Patrick Mahomes on Harrison Butker: I try to have confidence in everybody, I know he's working at it
sports.summary: Harrison Butker missed yet another field goal on Thursday night, which was a key factor in the Chiefs eventually losing to the Bills, 13-10.
sports.body:
With a whopping eight missed field goals in 11 games so far this season — plus one missed extra point — it’s fair to question how much longer the Chiefs can stick with their longtime kicker.

After the Thanksgiving loss, quarterback Patrick Mahomes offered some public support for the embattled kicker.

“I try to have confidence in everybody on the team. That’s part of playing this sport, is believing in the guys around you,” Mahomes said in his postgame press conference. “And obviously, Harrison hasn’t had the season that he’s wanted this year. But he’s also been one of the best kickers in the game for a long time.

“I know he’s working at it. I can tell you that. And he’s doing his best to be the best teammate he can be, and go out there and execute in those moments. Unfortunately, tonight it didn’t go his way. But, I promise you, he’ll come back and work at it again. And hopefully, the next time, he’ll be able to go out there and make it happen.”

The Chiefs signed Justin Tucker to their practice squad with the hope of pushing Butker to improve. But at this point, if Tucker is going to be around, it might be time to try him in a game.

Why not give something away? This is the week when everyone is trying to sell you something. No one is giving you anything, with zero strings attached.

On Our Way Home is primarily a Christmas story. It’s also a ghost story. I cranked it out between Thanksgiving and New Year’s Day a few years back.

In the interests of avoiding any spoilers, I’ll just say this: Download it and give it a try. It’s essentially about family and redemption and reconciliation. It’s also about forgiving others, while finding a way to forgive yourself.

It’s funny at times. It’s sad at times. If you make it to the end, you’ll possibly shed a tear or two.

The best feedback I’ve gotten came from a reader who had suffered from PTSD for years. Reading On Our Way Home unlocked his ability to feel emotions again.

I never intended anything like that. I just had an idea for a story, years before writing it. One year, I got caught up in the spirit of the season and it flowed, one chapter, one page, one word at a time.

The price is right. If you don’t like it, delete it. If you like it, keep going.

sports.title: Friday's game gives Steelers fans a chance to chime in on recent events

sports.body:
Later today, Steelers fans will get a chance to make their voices heard when the home team hosts the Broncos in a Black Friday game.

One option for Steelers fans will be to not show up. And we’ve heard some anecdotal evidence indicating that some fans have decided not to go to the game.

That may be better than the alternative. Steelers fans aren’t blindly loyal. If they see something they don’t like, they’ll make it known. Loudly.

The dynamic adds extra pressure to the situation. If things start poorly, you’ll hear the boos on the Prime Video stream, as clearly and plainly as we heard Rodgers’s comments during the Thursday night Prime Video game in Cleveland.

Last year, they booed during Renegade . Today, if the Steelers respond to the recent drama with a subpar showing, the booing will start a lot earlier than that strategic moment in the fourth quarter when they press “play” on their trademark rallying cry.

It’s just another reason to tune in at 3:00 p.m. ET, and to watch — and listen — closely.

sports.title: The "carnival" came back to town on Thursday, and Joe Milton III won his "teddy bear"
sports.summary: Cowboys' decision not to put Milton on the roster comes back to haunt them.
sports.body:
On Thursday, former Cowboys practice-squad quarterback Joe Milton III returned to Dallas and made them regret not putting him on the roster when they had the chance.

The Cowboys acquired Milton in April 2025 , sending a fifth-round pick to New England for Milton and a seventh-round pick. He appeared in four games last season before losing the training-camp and preseason competition with Sam Howell to be the backup to Dak Prescott.

Milton was released in late August. He cleared waivers. He joined the Dallas practice squad. After Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts landed on injured reserve due to blood clots, the Eagles came calling with a spot on the active roster. The Cowboys could have attempted to add Milton to their own active roster, but they didn’t.

Milton’s impressive performance has rekindled the comments made by Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer in the days before the 2026 rosters were cut from 90 to 53.

“I first remember hearing about Joe Milton he was at [the] University of Michigan, and everyone applauded him for how hard and how far he could throw the ball,” Schottenheimer said at the time, via Jane Slater of NFL Network. “Cool. That’s awesome. You know, go be in a carnival somewhere . Like, that’s not what playing NFL quarterback is. It’s not, ‘Yeah, I can throw the ball 85 yards.’ You’re throwing through small windows, you’re throwing over people, you’re changing arm slots. So, like, to me, arm strength is cool but, like, you know, go to the fair and win a teddy bear.”

In fairness to Schottenheimer, he then praised Milton’s development.

“But you got to play quarterback, you know, and that’s what I think you see Joe learning is he’s playing quarterback,” Schottenheimer said at the time. “And he’s playing quarterback at a high level. He’s checking the ball down. He’s making blitz adjustments. He’s solving problems. He’s reading, you know, from his first, second, to third and even fourth progression at times. And it takes time. I mean, it, you know, you don’t stop. I mean, you don’t stop learning as a quarterback and the only way to do it is to play and I’m really, really proud of him.”

Still, the Cowboys weren’t sufficiently proud of Milton to give him a roster spot. And owner/G.M. Jerry Jones refused to admit that they made a mistake.

sports.title: Bills benefited from extra seconds during Chiefs' final drive
sports.summary: For the second time this week, the clock operator took center stage.
sports.body:
We saw it on Monday night, when the clock operator didn’t press the button to save a second or two for the Bengals to try to pull out a win over the Commanders.

It apparently happened again on Thursday night, in more subtle fashion.

By our count, the Buffalo clock operator managed to preserve four seconds during what was the Chiefs’ final drive of the game.

I’ve watched it, several times. The Chiefs had first and 10 on their own 11. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes dropped the shotgun snap. By the time he recovered the ball, was touched, the whistle blew, and the Bills called a timeout (assuming they did it instantly), four seconds had elapsed. The clock, however, ultimately moved by only one second , from 26 to 25 — not 22.

Then, after running back Emmett Johnson gained five yards on second and 15, 19 seconds remained when the whistle blew. The clock in the NBC score bug at one point shifted from 19 seconds to 20, presumably to match the official time on the stadium scoreboard.

After the third-down incompletion, the clock showed 15 seconds. It should have been 11 seconds.

Following the punt, which was partially blocked, and the return by Greg Dortch, there were four seconds to play. Four seconds. The same four seconds that apparently were preserved through creative clock operation.

Of course, if the clock had shown 11 seconds and not 15 before the punt, the Bills may have not tried to block it. They may have opted to attempt a fair catch followed by a free kick.

sports.title: Zach Ertz: People don't understand how good DeVonta Smith is
sports.summary: Eagles wide receiver DeVonta Smith missed five games with a hamstring injury earlier this year and the Eagles lost all five of them, which doesn't feel like much of a coincidence after watching him in Dallas on Thursday.
sports.body:
Smith caught 11 passes for 200 yards and two touchdowns in Philadelphia’s remarkable 39-38 comeback win. The touchdowns came on 50- and 45-yard strikes from quarterback Joe Milton and Smith shook off a hard landing on his tailbone in the fourth quarter to finish out the game.

The 11 catches tied Smith’s career best and the 200 yards were a personal record, but the big day didn’t come as a shock to tight end Zach Ertz.

“It’s not surprising , honestly,” Ertz said, via Dave Zangaro of NBCSportsPhiladelphia.com. “I watched him when he was at Alabama, winning the Heisman. Comes in here right away, his game is just so smooth. I don’t think people understand how good of a player he truly is until he gets his opportunities. I don’t know what the final stats were. I know over 200 yards, which is crazy. But he’s just a receiver that really has no weakness. The way he runs routes is so smooth, the way he can make plays on the balls in the air, yards after catch. I think he’s probably one of the most underrated players in the league. I saw him as a rookie so where he’s at now doesn’t surprise me at all.”

The Eagles made Smith their No. 1 wideout when they traded A.J. Brown this offseason and the injury interrupted his bid to prove he’s the right guy to fill that role on their offense, but Thanksgiving offered some proof of concept for the Eagles’ passing game.

sports.summary: For all the records Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen has broken lately, this might be one that means a little more to him. After all, if you’ve listened to enough of Allen’s postgame press conferences, you know there’s one statistic he cares about more than any other — wins. With Buffalo’s 13-10
sports.body: For all the records Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen has broken lately, this might be one that means a little more to him. After all, if you’ve listened to enough of Allen’s postgame press conferences, you know there’s one statistic he cares about more than any other — wins. With Buffalo’s 13-10 win over the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night, Allen has now won 98 regular-season games, tying Russell Wilson for the most wins by a starting quarterback in his first nine NFL seasons. Wilson, who entered the league in 2012, never had a losing season during his first nine years with the Seattle Seahawks. He won double-digit games in eight of those nine seasons, including a career-high 13 in 2013. Allen, on the other hand, won just five games as a rookie in 2018. A year later, the Bills were back in the playoffs, and they haven’t had a losing season since. In fact, Buffalo extended its franchise record to eight consecutive winning seasons just last week with a win over the Miami Dolphins. Allen moved past Patrick Mahomes (95) on this particular list two weeks ago when the Bills beat the New York Jets. Now, having picked up another win at Mahomes’ expense, Allen has caught Wilson, too. Allen completed just 10-of-21 passes for 81 yards while adding 43 yards on the ground. The real hero of the night was Tyler Bass who scored seven of the team’s 13 points – including the game winning field goal from 57 yards. But football is a team sport, and Allen’s contribution still counts. And the win is his to claim. The Bills will be in New England next week, where Allen will have his first opportunity to take sole possession of the NFL record. Allen still has six regular-season games left in his ninth season. That gives him some time to make life a little more difficult for the next quarterback chasing this record.

sports.body: The New York Jets are 3-8. According to the NFL Playoff Picture (via the NFL Media Group), the Jets currently have a 1% chance of making the playoffs. If they lose to the Miami Dolphins in Week 12, that’ll reduce their chances to less than 1%. However, if they beat the fish, their playoff chances will double to 2%. Are you saying there’s a chance? There’s a section of the fan base that would prefer to see the Jets lose to both improve their draft positioning and to lessen the chances of Aaron Glenn returning in 2027. The problem, according to some of those fans, is that there are too many winnable games down the stretch for the Jets. On paper, the Jets will be or could be facing at least three backup quarterbacks (Carson Beck or Josh Johnson, Kyle McCord, and Tommy DeVito). Also, depending on whether the Buffalo Bills have anything left to play for in Week 18, that could be a fourth backup QB. Instead of complaining, why don’t we take advantage? This opens up a favorable pathway to go on a winning streak. Now, how likely is that? Well, that’s a different conversation altogether. The Jets haven’t won back-to-back games all season. They haven’t really upset anyone, and they haven’t consistently beaten teams that folks assume they should be able to beat. Both of those things would be necessary to even have a hint of the postseason. The other thing helping the Jets’ potential path is that the bottom of the AFC is falling apart. Pittsburgh is crumbling; the Jets have the head-to-head tiebreaker over Cleveland; they play New England; and Baltimore has a backup in at QB. I’m not saying it’s likely; I’m not guaranteeing it’s going to happen; all I’m saying is there’s a chance, and maybe that’s what Jets fans should be rooting for. The Indianapolis Colts are self-destructing. The Jets control their first-round pick. That pick has a great chance to be a top-three selection. sports.body: Late in the Buffalo Bills win over the Kansas City Chiefs, a turning point in the game was decided by replay. On third down inside two minutes, Patrick Mahomes found Rashee Rice over the middle of the field and Rice was popped by Bills safety Amani Hooker. As he fell to the ground, the ball moved. On the field it was ruled a catch. Because it was inside two minutes, the replay official had to call for a review and not Bills head coach Joe Brady. After replay, it was ruled an incomplete pass. After the game, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid addressed the play, saying he didn’t like the call. “Not one that I agreed with,” said Reid of the replay review. “This came from New York,” Reid said. “They called it a completion. I’m not quite sure what they saw, I saw he had control of the ball, and his elbow hit then the ball hit, but he had control. Normally, in those kind of situations, it has to be clear obvious. To me that was not clear and obvious.” The NBC broadcast spent a lot of time on it during the game and again in the postgame. Rules analyst Terry McAulay thought it was a catch and the Chiefs should have moved the chains. Cris Collinsworth talked about the laces on the ball, and when Rice hit the ground his hand moved down those laces while the ball touched the turf. I think it’s pretty clear the ball moved. His best season came in 2014 when he recorded 14.5 sacks and earned first-team All-Pro honors. Rousseau, now in his sixth NFL season, has spent his entire career in Buffalo after the Bills selected him with the 30th overall pick in the 2021 NFL Draft. Having already established a new personal single-season record for sacks this year, the 26 year old is now working his way through some familiar names in Buffalo’s history books. Once Rousseau gets past Mario Williams, there’s another Williams waiting for him. Former defensive tackle Kyle Williams (48.5), who spent all 13 of his NFL seasons in Buffalo, sits sixth on the franchise’s all-time list. With six regular-season games remaining, and the way Rousseau has been getting to opposing quarterbacks lately, we might not have to wait until next season to talk about him catching another Williams.

sports.title: Buffalo Bills RB James Cook ties 30-year-old NFL rushing record
sports.summary: Buffalo Bills running back James Cook III has a share of another NFL record. Cook has now rushed for at least 75 yards and a touchdown in 10 consecutive games, tying a record Terry Allen set across the 1995 and 1996 seasons with Washington. Cook found the end zone against the Kansas City Chiefs on [
sports.body: Buffalo Bills running back James Cook III has a share of another NFL record. Cook has now rushed for at least 75 yards and a touchdown in 10 consecutive games, tying a record Terry Allen set across the 1995 and 1996 seasons with Washington. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBillsPR/status/2126154593432178811?a=1zaXZ7gEe8A1q0j_ZqM&s=20] Cook found the end zone against the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night during the second quarter to put the Bills up 7-0. He then eclipsed the 75-yard mark in the third quarter on a five-yard run that put him at 79 for the night. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBills/status/2126135452583252133?a=kUYUD6G_ydbk91qANxM&s=20] It’s been 30 years since Allen put together his streak of 10 games. Since then, we’ve watched some pretty impressive running backs come through the NFL. LaDainian Tomlinson, Adrian Peterson, and Derrick Henry have all had their share of record-setting performances, but none of them managed to do what Cook just did. And unlike Allen, who needed parts of two seasons to put together his streak, Cook has done it all in the same season. In fact, the Bills’ season opener was the only game this year in which Cook didn’t meet both statistical requirements. Cook entered Thursday night’s game having rushed for 1,003 yards and 10 touchdowns over the course of his nine-game streak, averaging 111.4 yards per game and 5.1 yards per carry. He eclipsed the century mark in five of those nine games, including a season-high 157-yard performance against the New York Jets. Remember when we spent so much of the offseason in 2025 talking about whether the Bills should pay Cook? Buffalo eventually gave its running back a four-year, $48 million contract extension, and Cook has spent the better part of two seasons giving us reasons to talk about what a good decision that was. The Bills will head to Foxborough next week for their second meeting of the season with the New England Patriots. Cook rushed for 75 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in their first matchup. Another 75 yards and a trip to the end zone next week, and Cook will have an NFL record all to himself. Considering we’ve been watching him do just that every week since September, it might be time to start wondering just how big a number he’s going to leave for the next running back to chase.

sports.title: Jerry Jones on Mike McCarthy: "He was outstanding as the head coach"
sports.summary: The recent remarks from former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers regarding Steelers coach Mike McCarthy have raised plenty of questions, posed to plenty of people.
sports.body:
After Thursday’s 39-38 loss to the Eagles, Cowboys owner and G.M. Jerry Jones was asked about McCarthy, who coached Jones’s team for five seasons, from 2020 through 2024.

“I offered him to stay at least another year when he left,” Jones told reporters. “And so I thought he was outstanding as the head coach and had a great command of, frankly, quarterback, offense. Can’t say enough good things about him. He’s, frankly, one of the finest people that around football that I’ve been around. And I can’t say enough about him. I never had the type of thing that is being said about him. I never had that in consideration in any of my time with him, extending his contract. Any of that, that was never on the table. And we never had an issue within the organization.”

That conflicts, obviously, with the things Rodgers said on Wednesday.

Regardless, Jones no longer employs McCarthy. While Jones possibly chose to take the high road, a former employer vouching for a coach is fundamentally different than his current employer vouching for him.

McCarthy took the Cowboys to the playoffs three times in five years, advancing to the divisional round in 2022. The Cowboys failed to qualify for the postseason in the first year after McCarthy left. Thursday’s loss to the Eagles makes it harder for them to get there the second post-McCarthy season.

sports.title: Mike Tomlin on current Steelers situation: "It's a dumpster fire"
sports.summary: Former Steelers coach speaks at length about this week's events.
sports.body:
Appearing on NBC’s Chiefs-Bills halftime show on Thanksgiving night, Tomlin shared his thoughts on the situation in a conversation with Mike Tirico. (A portion of it was on the live broadcast; the full interview is here .)

“I had a range of emotions watching those course of events yesterday,” Tomlin told Tirico. “I think the prevailing one is just general sadness. Sad on a micro level, sad on a macro level. And by that, I mean, you know, just from an individual perspective, sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career of the quarterback, Aaron Rodgers, and just on the macro level, whether it’s organizationally or for the game of football at large, to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum.

“Those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football. So, just a lot of emotions, but probably more than anything, man, general sadness on a lot of levels.”

Tirico asked Tomlin if he was shocked by Rodgers’s decision to air dirty laundry in a public forum.

“It certainly did,” Tomlin said, “but, you know, and particularly because I know both men involved, certainly had a lot of intimate work and development of relationship with Aaron over the last couple of years, and have known and competed against Mike, you know, respected and appreciated him as a coach for a long time. But I don’t — what I acknowledge is I don’t know them as a collective, the nature of their relationships, and so certainly I was surprised by that.”

Regardless of Rodgers’s conduct on the way out the door, Tomlin explained that Rodgers was viewed favorably by his teammates in 2025.

“He was beloved, and I’m not, you know, over-exaggerating that,” Tomlin said. “He worked at it, and people appreciated his openness to getting to know and understand the Steeler culture, to be engaged with teammates, and particularly from my perspective, I worked with a lot of veteran players over the years and at times they lose a little patience for the process, or they lose patience for relationships with younger guys, et cetera. Man, he seemed to embrace all of that and really embrace it in a real, natural way. He was a tireless worker regarding the process.

“I called early-morning quarterback meetings on Wednesday and Thursday. He was always early and engaged. Did a heck of a job in terms of engaging and developing, assisting in the development of young players. Specifically, Will Howard was always in that meeting, and, shoot, man, [Rodgers] and I were shoulder-to-shoulder in terms of the development of Will and challenging Will to develop professional habits. And so, you know, it was early and extremely consistent during my time with him, in terms of his willingness to work in those areas, and I think that’s why he’s so beloved in that locker room, as been reported by multiple sources in light of this incident. That is real. The guys in that locker room love and appreciate Aaron Rodgers.”

sports.title: Bills lead Chiefs 7-3 at halftime on Thanksgiving night
sports.summary: Nasty weather in Western New York has limited offensive production for both Buffalo and Kansas City.
sports.body:
With steady freezing rain falling throughout the first half, it was difficult for both teams to get much going offensively. The game-time temperature was 35 degrees but the feels like temperature was down to 21.

The Bills have relied on running back James Cook for most of their offensive production. Cook rushed for 71 yards on 19 carries in the first half with a 5-yard touchdown.

Josh Allen is just 5-of-10 passing for 41 yards with an interception. Safety Alohi Gilman picked off Allen in the end zone on second-and-8 from the Kansas City 9 midway through the second quarter. At that point, it seemed like if the Bills scored a touchdown, they might have an insurmountable lead.

While the Chiefs didn’t score off of that interception, they at least kept Buffalo off the board.

But Kansas City had several miscues from the wet ball. The team had trouble fielding kicks, punter Matt Ariza had trouble catching a long snap before a punt, and Patrick Mahomes had trouble fielding a snap.

But Kansas City finally got a little something going late in the second quarter, with Harrison Butker sending a 26-yard field goal through the uprights to narrow Buffalo’s lead to four points.

Through 30 minutes, Mahomes is 10-of-15 for 97 yards. Travis Kelce has four receptions for 71 yards, including a key 21-yard catch at the end of the first half to get Kansas City into scoring position.

sports.title: James Cook touchdown gives Bills 7-0 lead over Chiefs
sports.summary: There is some nasty weather in Western New York on Thanksgiving night.
sports.body:
The Bills have at least scored one early in the second quarter, with James Cook going in for a 5-yard score.

It took Buffalo 11 plays to go 49 yards, with the team getting great field positions as a result of one play on special teams.

Chiefs returner Josh Downs let a punt fall and roll instead of fielding it in his team’s territory, which led the offense to start its second drive at the 4-yard line. Kansas City then went three-and-out, and the punt went out of bounds at the Kansas City 49.

The Bills only needed to convert one third down on their ensuing drive, with Josh Allen hitting Khaliil Shakir for a 17-yard pass on third-and-6.

While Buffalo got down to the 1-yard line, a false start backed them up. but Cook then erased that with his touchdown run.

In three drives, Cook has 42 yards on 13 carries with one touchdown. Allen is just 3-of-6 passing for 30 yards.

sports.body: Tonight, one of the NFL’s biggest games of the 2026 NFL season plays out in Orchard Park, NY. The Buffalo Bills take on the Kansas City Chiefs tonight for a Thanksgiving Day game in primetime. This is the first time the Bills are hosting a game on Thanksgiving, and it comes against one of their biggest rivals — and what many believe to be the best rivalry in sports today. At 9-1, Buffalo is currently in first place in the AFC and in control of their playoff fate. If the regular season ended today, the Bills would claim the one seed and a bye to begin the postseason. If the current standings prevail, the 8-2 Chiefs would be the five seed, and playing at the Cincinnati Bengals in the Wild Card round. Tonight’s game isn’t isn’t of the elimination variety because there’s a lot more football yet to play, but there’s a lot at stake for both the winner and loser. If Buffalo loses they’d surrender a head-to-head advantage to Kansas City, and sole possession of first place in the conference. While many in Chiefs Kingdom are quick to remind Bills Mafia that regular-season wins don’t really matter, that couldn’t be further from the truth. You can be sure that quarterbacks Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes know how big this game is for their seasons. Will Allen and the Bills take down the Chiefs in head coach Joe Brady’s first matchup leading the team against Andy Reid and Steve Spagnuolo? When Buffalo and Kansas City square off, anything’s possible! However, remember that the weather might have a say in how this one plays out. Here’s your open thread for Bills-Chiefs on Thanksgiving night. As always, be kind to each other — and in all things… go Bills!

sports.title: Aaron Rodgers clears waivers
sports.summary: Rodgers becomes a free agent.
sports.body:
For the third time since March 2025, Rodgers can sign with any team at any time.

The soon-to-be 43-year-old cleared waivers on Thursday, per multiple reports.

He can sign whenever he chooses, either to a practice squad or a 53-man roster. He can wait until the postseason, if he chooses.

Of course, someone will have to want to sign him. In the 2026 offseason, only the Steelers did. At this point, an injury to a starter on a contending team will be the one thing that could create immediate interest in his services.

As long as that team is willing to risk Rodgers eventually dialing up McAfee for another elongated monologue of grievances. At this point, any other outcome would be a surprise.

sports.title: Art Rooney II expresses support for Mike McCarthy, calls Aaron Rodgers not a "good teammate"
sports.summary: Steelers owner speaks about Wednesday's insanity.
sports.body:
Steelers owner Art Rooney II has addressed the events that resulted in the benching and then the firing of quarterback Aaron Rodgers.

“A change had to be made , and I certainly agree with the change and the way it was handled,” Rooney told Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette in a Thursday interview.

The change was sparked by the notion that Rodgers gave coach Mike McCarthy an ultimatum: “Either let me call all the plays or just release me.” Instead, McCarthy benched him.

It went to the next level when, as many expected, Rodgers scurried to the McAfee show to take shots at McCarthy for missing meetings, showing up late to meetings, and falling asleep in meetings — among other things, including the ultra-embarrassing “1-2-3 Packers!” moment from halftime of Sunday’s loss to the Eagles.

“There’s maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload,” Rooney said. “He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don’t do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that’s for sure. . . .

“In general, I think, historically, what’s in the locker room stays in the locker room. That’s the way it’s always been. That’s the way it should be as far as I’m concerned.”

Rooney also confirmed that the team supports McCarthy, despite Rodgers’s rant and reports confirming the facts underpinning the petty delivery of them.

“I just want to say that I have 100 [percent] confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond,” Rooney told Dulac. “The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.”

sports.body: The Jets have played eight times on Thanksgiving in the past. They are an even 4-4 in those games. Below we will take a look at them. November 24, 1960: New York Titans 41 Dallas Texans 35 The American Football League played games on Thanksgiving, and the Jets played on Turkey Day in each their first three years of existence. They were called the Titans at that point. Playing against the future Kansas City Chiefs, Don Maynard caught 10 passes for 179 yards and a touchdown, while Art Powell added 8 catches for 110 yards and a touchdown. November 23, 1961: New York Titans 21 Buffalo Bills 14 Al Dorow threw for 223 yards and a touchdown, and Dick Felt returned an interception 55 yards for a touchdown to provide the Titans with the winning margin at the Polo Grounds. November 22, 1962: New York Titans 46 Denver Broncos 45 A wild game in Denver saw the Titans blow a 24-7 lead and then overcome a 45-32 fourth quarter deficit on Johnny Green’s fourth and fifth touchdown passes of the game, one to Dick Christy and the other to Art Powell. November 23, 1972: Detroit Lions 37 New York Jets 20 Entering the fourth quarter, the Lions led 23-20, but they blew the game open with a field goal and touchdown runs by Greg Landry from 6 yards and Altie Taylor from 38. November 28, 1985: Detroit Lions 31 New York Jets 20 Eric Hipple threw four touchdown passes, three to Leonard Thompson as the Lions jumped out to a 24-3 lead and never looked back. November 22, 2007: Dallas Cowboys 34 New York Jets 3 It was an ugly afternoon in a lost season for the Jets. The Cowboys owned a 21-3 lead at halftime on a Marion Barber touchdown run, a Jason Witten reception from Tony Romo, and a Terrence Newman interception off Kellen Clemens returned for a score. November 25, 2010: New York Jets 26 Cincinnati Bengals 10 In the third meeting between these teams in eleven months, the Jets erased a 10-7 halftime deficit. Brad Smith was the star with a 53 yard touchdown run in the first minute of the second half and an 89 yard kickoff returned for a score in the fourth quarter. November 22, 2012: New England Patriots 49 New York Jets 19 This game is best remembered for the Buttfumble. What people don’t remember was that was part of a 52 second span where New England scored an offensive touchdown, a defensive touchdown, and a special teams touchdown to turn a 7-0 lead into a 28-0 rout.

sports.title: Why do the Lions and Cowboys always play on Thanksgiving?
sports.summary: There are three NFL games today. The Lions host the Bears, the Cowboys host the Eagles, and the Bills host the Chiefs. The teams playing the night game change annually, but you might notice that the Lions always host the first game of the day, and the Cowboys always host the second game. How did […]
sports.body: There are three NFL games today. The Lions host the Bears, the Cowboys host the Eagles, and the Bills host the Chiefs. The teams playing the night game change annually, but you might notice that the Lions always host the first game of the day, and the Cowboys always host the second game. How did that come to be? The Lions played their first Thanksgiving game in 1934. It was their first season in Detroit. They had previously been located in Portsmouth, Ohio, where they were known as the Portsmouth Spartans. A radio executive named George Richards bought the franchise and moved it to Detroit. The Lions were having difficulty gaining any sort of popularity in their new home city. Richards came up with the idea of scheduling their team’s big game against the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving. The Lions were 10-1 at the time, and the Bears were 11-0. This was before the days when the league dictated the schedule to its teams. The teams themselves could schedule the times of their games. Richards used his connections in the radio business to get the game broadcast nationally. Even thought Detroit lost, it was a huge success. The Lions sold the game out, and they have played on Thanksgiving ever since with the exception of World War II years despite some calls for them to lose the game during the dismal Matt Millen Era. Thanksgiving gained a second traditional team in 1951. For the next thirteen years, the Green Bay Packers traveled to Detroit to play the Lions on Thanksgiving. Vince Lombardi ended the arrangement. Lombardi cited the end of an agreement that paid the Packers $10,000 extra for playing the game, the difficulties of playing games on a short week every year, and having to face a rival in front of an electric crowd on the road every season. Of course since the teams are in the same division, the Packers remain a frequent Thanksgiving opponent for Detroit. So how about the Cowboys? In the mid-1960’s the NFL was looking to add a second Thanksgiving game. It was not entirely clear it would work outside Detroit, where Thanksgiving NFL was already a tradition. The Dallas Cowboys were a six year old team with no history of winning. General manager Tex Schramm was a visionary.
